business_problem: Large warehouses need faster, more efficient operations, but manually tailoring each warehouse management system and assigning transport orders sequentially or by exhaustively testing options slows delivery, raises costs, and limits throughput.
solution_summary: KION describes an in-house AI implementation for intralogistics that combines Generative AI (GenAI), warehouse management systems (WMS), and genetic algorithms. GenAI is used during planning and deployment to turn a detailed description of a warehouse's processes and structures into a customized WMS configuration, reducing the manual engineering effort normally required for each unique site. The same AI-assisted workflow also automates test runs and documentation, helping standardize implementations and reduce human error. In live warehouse operations, genetic algorithms act as the optimization engine for fleet control: they rapidly evaluate many transport-order allocation patterns and select near-best assignments instead of processing orders rigidly one by one or trying every possible combination. The resulting WMS-driven control loop improves resource use, throughput, responsiveness to changing conditions, and overall warehouse efficiency.

solution_components.name: Generative AI (GenAI)
solution_components.role: Automatically configures a customized WMS from detailed warehouse process and structure descriptions and automates test runs and documentation.

solution_components.name: warehouse management systems (WMS)
solution_components.role: Runs the warehouse-specific control logic produced through AI-assisted configuration for planning, implementation, and operation.

solution_components.name: genetic algorithms
solution_components.role: Optimize transport-order allocation for warehouse fleet control in fractions of a second during operations.

data_flow: Detailed descriptions of warehouse processes and structures are fed into Generative AI to create a customized WMS configuration. During deployment, the same AI automates testing and documentation. In operations, incoming transport orders are evaluated by genetic algorithms, which score allocation options and pass near-best assignments into the WMS-driven fleet control process for warehouse vehicle movements.
integration_points: Detailed descriptions of warehouse processes and structures
business_outcome: KION reports faster planning, implementation, and operation of warehouse software, more standardized and higher-quality WMS adaptations with fewer human errors, and real-time fleet control that increases capacity utilization and throughput while reducing warehouse operating costs.
